question.text: A thin film of soap solution <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>s</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.4</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> lies on the top of a glass plate <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><msub><mrow><mi>μ</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1.5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>. When visible light is incident almost normal to the plate, two wavelengths <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>420</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>630</mn><mo> </mo><mi>nm</mi></math> are strongly reflected. What is the minimum thickness (in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>nm</mi></math>) of the soap film?

solution.text:
For reflection at the air - soap solution interface, the phase difference is π



For reflection at the interface of soap solution to glass also, there will be a phase difference of π

∴   The condition for the maximum intensity

=  2μt=nλ

For n, nλ1=n-1 λ2

n×420=n-1630

∴     n630-420=630

⇒    n210=630

⇒    n=630210

⇒ n=3

This is the maximum order, where they coincide

2×1.4×t=3×420

⇒   t=3×4202×1.40=450 nm
